stem.en: Kabir asks why the lysosome's cutters do not "escape and eat the cell". What keeps them safe?

text.en: Two things. They are in their own bubble of wall, so they cannot reach the rest of the cell. And they only work in acid; the cell outside the bag is pH 7.2, where they would barely cut even if they leaked.

feedback.en: They float freely inside the bag. The bag's wall and its pH are the safety.
They cut proteins, fats and sugars of any origin. Spill them at the right pH and they would cut the cell.

text.en: The cell is made of stuff they cannot cut.

feedback.en: The cell is proteins, fats and sugars, exactly what they cut. The bag and its acid are what stand between.

explanation.en: Two safeties, both from earlier Books. A room of wall, from V.1, and a pH the cutters need, from III.7. A cell that dies often kills itself by spilling these bags.
